title: Raw HTML Output Leading to XSS
platform_conditions: ASP.NET (MVC/Razor) and Blazor; applies to any view engine with Razor-style auto-encoding plus explicit opt-out APIs
security_mechanism: Razor encodes every emitted expression unless the developer marks the string as trusted. Html.Raw (Razor), HtmlString/MarkupString, and IHtmlContent-typed properties short-circuit that encoder, so markup in the string is parsed as HTML by the browser; a stored value containing <script> or an event-handler attribute therefore executes in every victim's session. The encoded-opt-out also covers attribute and javascript:-URL positions the default encoder does not reach when the value is already an IHtmlContent.

source_sink_clues.source: Stored user content (bios, comments, rich-text fields), request parameters echoed back, and any third-party HTML accepted into the content pipeline.
source_sink_clues.sink: @Html.Raw(...), new HtmlString(...), [MarkupString]-decorated Blazor fields, and direct @model-to-IHtmlContent assignments rendered into a page

tracking_guards: Check whether the raw-markup path runs untrusted content through a sanitizer with an allowlist policy before rendering; check the content is produced by the server from fixed templates rather than user text; in attribute and URL positions require scheme validation (http/https only) even for trusted fragments.
not_candidate_when: The string is server-generated markup from a fixed template with no user-derived fragment, an allowlist sanitizer (with a hardened policy) processes the content before Raw, or the field only ever holds values written by trusted administrators within a trusted-content model.
public_references: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html
OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
